instruction: Count the number of PDF files in ~/Documents/Papers/ and save just the number to ~/pdf_count.txt.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to extract first authors from 4 PDFs and create Excel table. Installed poppler-utils, converted PDFs to text, read author info, started writing Python/openpyxl script but ran out of 50 turns before completing the xlsx file. Also misidentified first author of zhang_appagent.pdf.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open terminal, install packages (apt-get), use pdftotext to convert PDFs, read text files with head/grep, write Python scripts in terminal, use openpyxl for Excel creation
metadata.failure_analysis: Model spent too many turns on installation waits and type+Enter cycles. Misidentified first author of AppAgent paper (Gang Yu instead of Chi Zhang). Ran out of 50-turn limit before saving the xlsx file.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplest possible file operation task - just count PDFs and write the number. Tests basic terminal + file creation with no parsing. Well within demonstrated capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires counting PDF files and writing the number to a text file. Getter reads the text file from VM, metric checks the content contains the expected number '4'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads ~/pdf_count.txt from the VM and returns content as a dict with 'content' key
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as rules dict directly (expected.get('expected_count') = '4'), consistent with type='rule' framework behavior
Expected value '4' matches the exactly 4 PDF files set up in the config
Single instruction requirement (count PDFs and save number) is fully covered by the evaluator
Minor leniency: regex \d+ could match '4' inside larger numbers like '14' or '42', but the instruction says 'save just the number' so this is unlikely to cause false positives in practice
